First, we find the derivative of $f(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
{f}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{cos}^{2}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t+7)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ -10\operatorname{cos}⁡t\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ -5\operatorname{sin}⁡2t \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$

Next, we calculate ${f}^{″}(t)$ by differentiating ${f}^{′}(t):$

$$
{f}^{″}(t)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-5\operatorname{sin}⁡2t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -10\operatorname{cos}⁡2t \\ -2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, we find ${f}^{″}(0)$ by substituting $t=0$ into the above:

$$
{f}^{″}(0)=[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡0+\operatorname{cos}⁡0 \\ -10\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0) \\ -2\operatorname{sin}⁡0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-0+1 \\ -10(1) \\ -2(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -10 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$
